title: what tantra actually is
tomorrow: why would worship start by touching your own body?

segments.voice: Yesterday, what tantra actually is, by one book's account: a mercy for a hurried age. Today, that same book walks into an ordinary house.

Six in the morning, and a dad is already three things at once: packing a lunch, listening to his mother on speaker, hunting for a lost shoe. Someone knocks. A neighbor needs a hand. His coffee goes cold on the counter. Is this the spiritual life, or the thing keeping him from it? The Mahanirvana Tantra stops, in the middle of Shiva's answer to the goddess, to describe this man: a grihastha, a householder.
screen: `SIX A.M., THREE JOBS AT ONCE.` → `A KNOCK. COLD COFFEE.` → `THE PATH, OR IN THE WAY?`

segments.voice: The householder Shiva describes is devoted to Brahman, the highest reality, and still fully at home. He works, and works honestly. He keeps his speech truthful. He honors his mother and father, and the text treats them as gods a person can actually see. He cares for his spouse and his children. Guests are welcomed, not tolerated. And the thread through all of it: whatever he does, he offers to Brahman. So the cold coffee has its answer. In a book that calls itself a Tantra, the house itself is the place of practice. Nobody is sent to a cave. The duties of an ordinary day aren't a detour on the way to the highest; they're part of the road. Some readers hear an echo of an older line on this path, from the Bhagavad Gita: whatever you do, offer it. This book carries that idea home, to the kitchen and the doorway. Tantra has a reputation for the forbidden and the secret. Here it is in a lunchbox and an open door. So one more answer to what tantra actually is, from one text: a path that doesn't ask a householder to stop being one.
screen: `A GRIHASTHA: FULLY AT HOME.` · `PARENTS: GODS YOU CAN SEE.` · `EVERY ACT OFFERED TO BRAHMAN.` · `THE HOUSE IS THE PLACE OF PRACTICE.` · then, large: `A LUNCHBOX AND AN OPEN DOOR.`

segments.voice: If you can, stand and walk slowly for part of the sit, to a sink, a door or a window, as if the walk itself were an offering. If you're staying put, rest your hands open and bring to mind one ordinary task waiting today, offered before it's begun.
What tantra actually is: here, a path the Mahanirvana Tantra lays through a householder's day, every act offered.
Hold on to it: what tantra actually is, a house that is the place of practice. Day sixteen-eighteen.

howItsDone: Some Hindu families in tantric and Shakta lineages see household duties as part of their practice, and teachers draw on the Mahanirvana Tantra's householder chapters when they speak about family life.

fork.setup: your friend says she'll start her spiritual life once her kids are grown and the house is quiet. what does the Mahanirvana's householder suggest?
options: the house is already the place of practice, every act offered.
she's right: family duties are a detour from the highest.
she should step away now; real practice needs a quiet cave.
fork.reveal: Shiva's householder works, cares for parents, spouse, children and guests, and offers all of it to Brahman. nobody is sent to a cave.

original.note: Sanskrit: one who stands in the house; a householder.
